mainTopic: Whether purity depends on קפידא, and the dispute between רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ and רבי יוחנן over whether absorbed impure liquid makes things טמא before it comes out.
overview: רבי אבא asks רב אשי whether purity really depends on קפידא, whether the owner minds a stain. רב אשי says yes. He proves it from רבי חייא: even definite נדה blood is nullified once the seven cleaning substances are applied. The גמרא then quotes a משנה in כלים: a זב's pottery soaked with impure liquid falls into an oven, and once the oven is heated, the oven is טמא. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says severe liquids make the oven טמא even without heating. רבי יוחנן says heating is always needed, because absorbed liquid does not count until it comes out. רבי יוחנן challenges him from stains, from רבי חייא, and from corpse blood absorbed in a garment. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's side answers that those cases are rabbinic, or rejects the source. Then רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה about absorbed liquid. רב פפא answers by sorting the cases by whether the liquid can come out and whether the owner cares. His explanation of רבי יוחנן's reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does it all depend on whether the owner minds the stain?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב אשי whether, according to his earlier ruling about the washed stain, purity really depends on קפידא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רב אשי: Is the whole matter really dependent on whether a person is particular about the stain?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is questioning the logic behind רב אשי's earlier ruling about a stain that was washed with the cleaning substances. He wants to know whether רב אשי really means that purity depends on whether the owner cares about the mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's ruling seemed to treat the stain differently depending on whether the owner still minded it. רבי אבא finds that surprising. Normally we would expect the physical presence of blood to decide purity, not a person's attitude toward it.

keyTerms.meaning: Being particular, minding something (here, minding a stain)
Is it then...? (an opening word that expresses surprise)
The matter depends (on)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi:
Does the matter depend on being particular?
phrases.notes: He means: does purity hinge on whether the owner still minds the stain, rather than on whether blood is still there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind רב אשי's ruling from the previous part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether purity of a stained garment truly depends on the owner's קפידא and not just on whether blood is physically present.

steps.title: Yes, as רבי חייא taught about real נדה blood
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers yes and cites רבי חייא: definite נדה blood is nullified once the seven substances are applied to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי חייא says: blood that is definitely נדה blood, one applies the seven substances to it and nullifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says yes, it does depend on קפידא. He brings a ברייתא of רבי חייא as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא rules that even certain נדה blood is 'nullified' once the seven cleaning substances have been put on it, even if a mark still remains. That is the raw material for רב אשי's proof, which he spells out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Blood that is definitely from a נדה
The seven cleaning substances listed in the משנה
He nullifies it, so it no longer counts as a stain

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
as it is taught: Rabbi Ḥiyya says:
Blood that is certainly of a menstruating woman —
one applies the seven substances to it,
phrases.notes: These are the seven cleaning materials listed in the משנה on this daf.

phrases.english: and nullifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question with a yes and brings a supporting ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, purity depends on קפידא, as shown by רבי חייא's ruling that even definite נדה blood is nullified by the seven substances.

steps.title: The blood is still there, so it must depend on קפידא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי spells out the proof: since real נדה blood can be nullified, the deciding factor must be whether the owner minds it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why should it be pure? It is נדה blood! Clearly the matter depends on being particular. So too here, the matter depends on being particular.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why רבי חייא's ruling proves his point. He then applies that conclusion to his own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what is left is truly נדה blood, it should make the garment טמא. Yet רבי חייא says it is nullified. So the deciding factor cannot be the blood itself. Once the seven substances have been tried, the owner no longer minds the leftover mark, and that is what makes the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: But why?
Evidently, this shows that
So too (in our case)

steps.whatToRemember: A stain's purity status can depend on קפידא. Even definite נדה blood is nullified after the seven substances are applied, because the owner no longer minds what is left.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the leftover mark stops being blood in a physical sense. The point is that a mark nobody minds anymore is halachically disregarded.

phrases.english: But why? It is blood of a menstruating woman!
Evidently the matter depends on being particular,
so too here the matter depends on being particular.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the reasoning from רבי חייא's ברייתא and applies it to רב אשי's case.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's position that purity depends on קפידא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ברייתא that definite נדה blood is nullified by the seven substances, which only makes sense if קפידא is the deciding factor.

steps.title: A זב's pottery falls into an oven that is then heated
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: a משנה in כלים rules that an oven becomes טמא when a זב's pottery, soaked with impure liquid, falls inside and the oven is heated.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: pottery that a זב used, which absorbed liquids, and which fell into the airspace of an oven, and the oven was then heated: the oven is טמא, because the liquid will eventually come out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from מסכת כלים. This sets up a discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pottery has absorbed the זב's impure liquid. When the oven is heated, that liquid is expected to seep out into the oven, so the oven is ruled טמא. The ruling treats what will eventually come out as if it is already coming out.

keyTerms.meaning: Earthenware pieces or vessels (here, a chamber pot)
A man with a gonorrhea-like discharge, who is a source of impurity
Liquids (here, the זב's impure fluids)
The airspace inside the oven
Because the liquid will eventually come out

phrases.english: We learned there:
Pottery that a zav used,
that absorbed liquids,
and fell into the airspace of the oven,
and the oven was heated —
the oven is impure,
because the liquid will eventually come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the קפידא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oven becomes טמא when a זב's pottery that absorbed impure liquid falls into its airspace and the oven is then heated, because the liquid will eventually come out.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits the oven ruling to light liquids
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says the משנה's heating requirement applies only to light impure liquids. Severe impure liquids make the oven טמא even without heating.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The משנה only taught this about light liquids. But with severe liquids, the oven is impure even though it was not heated.
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ explains the oven משנה from the previous step. He says the rule 'only if the oven was heated' is limited to light impure liquids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Light liquids are only weakly טמא, so they make the oven טמא only when the heat pushes them out of the pottery. Severe liquids (like those of the זב himself) are a strong source of טומאה. They make the oven טמא right away, even while still soaked inside the pottery.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about...': a phrase that limits a משנה to a narrower case
Light liquids: liquids with a weaker level of טומאה
Severe liquids: liquids that are a strong source of טומאה, like those of a זב
Was heated (the oven was fired up)

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about light liquids,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the oven rule from the משנה: the oven becomes טמא once it is heated.

phrases.english: but with severe liquids, it is impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַּק הַתַּנּוּר.
phrases.english: even though the oven was not heated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַשְׁקִין קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the oven משנה cited in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Severe impure liquids absorbed in pottery make the oven טמא even without heating. Only light liquids need the heating.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: heating is needed for both kinds of liquids
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. For both light and severe liquids, the oven is טמא only if it was heated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Both light liquids and severe liquids are the same. If the oven was heated, yes, it is impure. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view. He says the heating requirement applies to every kind of impure liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a liquid soaked deep inside pottery does not count while it stays hidden there, no matter how strong its טומאה is. Only when the heat makes it come out can it make the oven טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Both this and that': the two cases are treated the same
Yes (Aramaic)
If not, then no

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מַשְׁקִין קַלִּין וְאֶחָד מַשְׁקִין חֲמוּרִין,
phrases.english: Both light liquids and severe liquids:
if the oven was heated, yes, it is impure;
if not, then no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֶחָד מַשְׁקִין קַלִּין וְאֶחָד מַשְׁקִין חֲמוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's limitation in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Absorbed impure liquids of any kind make the oven טמא only once the heat brings them out.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says severe liquids make the oven טמא even while hidden inside the pottery. רבי יוחנן says hidden liquids never count until the heat brings them out.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from the stain that would not wash out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ from the משנה about a stain that stayed even after the seven substances were applied. The טהרות are טהור and the garment needs no new immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן objected to ריש לקיש: If he immersed the garment, handled pure foods on it, then applied the seven substances and the stain did not come out, it is a dye. His pure foods stay pure, and he does not need to immerse it again!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה to attack רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. A stain that is stuck deep in a garment does not make things טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the stain is really blood, it is soaked in so deeply that it will not come out, and the משנה ignores it. This matches רבי יוחנן's rule that absorbed טומאה which does not come out does not count. That goes against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, who says absorbed severe liquids are טמא even while hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed it (in a מקוה)
Ritually pure foods or items
The seven cleaning substances used to test a stain
Dye

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
If he immersed it and handled pure items on it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a garment with a stain whose source is unknown.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶעֱבִיר עָלָיו שִׁבְעָה סַמָּנִין וְלֹא עָבַר —
phrases.english: and then applied the seven substances to it and it did not come out,
this is a dye, and his pure items are pure,
and he does not need to immerse it again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן attacks רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's view from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's ruling that absorbed severe טומאה counts even when it does not come out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows that a stain stuck deep in a garment, which will not come out, is ignored. So absorbed טומאה should not count until it comes out.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: stains are only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answers that stains are טמא only מדרבנן, so the Sages could be lenient there. That does not prove anything about Torah-level liquids.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Leave aside stains, which are only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ pushes the proof away. He says the stain case is different because its טומאה is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כתמים are only דרבנן, the Sages were free to be lenient and ignore a stain that does not come out. The severe liquids in the oven case are טמא מדאורייתא, so there is no reason to say the same leniency applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside: you cannot bring a proof from that case
Stains (of blood found on a garment)
Rabbinic: a law made by the Sages, not directly from the Torah

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside stains, which are rabbinic.
phrases.notes: He means a rabbinic case can't prove a Torah-level case, because the Sages could choose to be lenient here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stain case shows that absorbed טומאה that does not come out is always ignored.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only rabbinic stains get this leniency. Torah-level impure liquids may still be טמא while absorbed.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי חייא: even definite נדה blood is nullified
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן counters with רבי חייא's teaching. Even definite נדה blood, which is טמא מדאורייתא, is nullified by the seven substances.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא teach: With blood that is definitely from a נדה, one applies the seven substances to it and nullifies it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's answer. He argues that the same leniency applies to Torah-level blood too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ said the leniency is only for rabbinic stains. But רבי חייא speaks of definite נדה blood, which is טמא מדאורייתא, and it is still nullified once it is stuck in the garment. So the 'rabbinic only' answer does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a woman who is a נדה, a Torah-level source of טומאה
Definitely, for certain
He nullifies it, so it no longer counts

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same teaching of רבי חייא quoted back in step 2. Here the גמרא uses it for a new purpose: to show the leniency is not just rabbinic.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya teach:
Blood that is definitely from a niddah:
one applies the seven substances to it and nullifies it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: דַּם הַנִּדָּה וַדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's claim that the stain leniency applies only because stains are rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Definite נדה blood is טמא מדאורייתא, yet it is still nullified when it stays stuck in the garment. So absorbed Torah-level טומאה can also be ignored.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rejects Rabbi Chiya's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says רבי חייא's teaching cannot be used against him. If רבי did not teach it in the משנה, how could רבי חייא know it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי did not teach this. So where would רבי חייא get it from?
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answers רבי יוחנן's last challenge. He refuses to accept רבי חייא's teaching as a real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא was a student of רבי, who put together the משנה. If the משנה does not say that Torah-level נדה blood is cancelled by the seven substances, a student of רבי would not teach something different. So רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ treats that teaching as unreliable, and the proof from step 9 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: did not teach (it in the משנה)
from where does he know it?

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name after it is not a general title. It always means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rebbi did not teach it,
phrases.notes: רבי did not put this ruling in the משנה.

phrases.english: from where would Rabbi Chiya know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי לֹא שָׁנָה, רַבִּי חִיָּיא מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source used in the challenge of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי חייא's teaching about definite נדה blood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching goes against what רבי's משנה includes. A student of רבי would not teach something the משנה does not contain.

steps.title: New challenge: blood absorbed in a house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן starts a new challenge from a משנה. A רביעית of blood absorbed into a house makes the house טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: A רביעית of blood that was absorbed into a house makes the house impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins quoting a new משנה to challenge רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. This first part sets up the challenge; the real point comes with the garment case a little later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about blood from a dead body that soaked into the floor of a house. It rules that the house, meaning the vessels inside it, is טמא. The גמרא first comments on this line, and then the משנה goes on to the garment case.

keyTerms.meaning: a quarter of a לוג, the amount of corpse blood that makes things טמא
absorbed, soaked in
ritually impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:
A quarter-log of blood
phrases.notes: This is blood from a dead body, so it can make a whole house impure.

phrases.english: that was absorbed into a house —
the house is impure,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי חייא's teaching was rejected, רבי יוחנן brings a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's view that severe impure liquids count even when absorbed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the opening of a משנה whose garment case will show that absorbed corpse blood does not count.

steps.title: Two versions of the house ruling are reconciled
steps.stepSummary: Some have the reading 'the house is טהור.' The גמרא explains that the two readings do not argue. One is about vessels that were there from the start, and the other is about vessels brought in later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the ruling is: the house is pure. But they don't really disagree. 'Impure' is about vessels that were there from the beginning. 'Pure' is about vessels that came in at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: In a side comment, the גמרא brings up a second version of the משנה and shows that both versions are correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels that were in the house before the blood soaked in become טמא. Vessels that came in only after the blood had already soaked in stay טהור. The point of רבי יוחנן's challenge comes in the משנה's next line, about the garment.

keyTerms.meaning: they do not disagree
from the beginning
at the end

phrases.english: And some say: the house is pure.
And they do not disagree —
this one is about vessels that were there from the beginning,
that one is about vessels that came at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: הַבַּיִת טָהוֹר. וְלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment on the line of the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different vessels at different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two readings of the משנה seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vessels there from the start are טמא. Vessels that came after the blood was absorbed are טהור.

steps.title: Blood absorbed in a garment counts only if it washes out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: blood absorbed in a garment makes it טמא only if washing brings out a רביעית. Otherwise it is טהור. This goes against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood soaked into a garment: if the garment is washed and a רביעית of blood comes out, it is impure. If not, it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main point of רבי יוחנן's challenge. Corpse blood that stays absorbed in a garment does not make it טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Corpse blood is a severe, Torah-level impurity. Yet the משנה says absorbed blood counts only if it can come out. That goes against רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, who said severe liquids make an oven טמא even without being drawn out by heat.

keyTerms.meaning: a garment
is washed (laundered)
ritually pure

phrases.english: If it was absorbed into a garment,
if it is washed
and a quarter-log of blood comes out of it —
it is impure,
and if not — it is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִבְלְעָה בִּכְסוּת, אִם מִתְכַּבֶּסֶת וְיוֹצֵא מִמֶּנָּה רְבִיעִית דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 11 and gives the actual challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's ruling (step 5) that severe impure liquids make something טמא even without being drawn out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah-level corpse blood that stays absorbed in a garment is טהור. So absorbed severe liquids do not count unless they come out, just like רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: רב כהנא: this is rabbinic blood, so the Sages were lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that this ruling is one of the leniencies of רביעיות. It is about דם תבוסה, which is only טמא מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: They taught here one of the leniencies of רביעית measures. דם תבוסה is different, because its impurity is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. He explains that the garment case is a special leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment case is about דם תבוסה, which is only טמא מדרבנן. Since the Sages made it טמא, they could also make it טהור when it is absorbed. This works the same way as the stains answer in step 8, and it says nothing about Torah-level liquids.

keyTerms.meaning: the leniencies that apply to רביעית measures
it is different
'blood of submission,' blood that comes out of a person at the time of death
of rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: Twice, when רבי יוחנן brings a case where absorbed impurity is treated leniently, רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's side answers that the case is only rabbinic (stains in step 8, דם תבוסה here). רבי חייא's teaching was handled differently: it was rejected outright in step 10. According to רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, Torah-level severe liquids still make an oven טמא even without heating.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a leniency in a rabbinic impurity cannot be used to prove a rule about Torah-level impurity.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
They taught here one of the leniencies of quarter-log measures,
blood of submission is different, since it is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקּוּלֵּי רְבִיעִיּוֹת שָׁנוּ כָּאן, שָׁאנֵי דַּם תְּבוּסָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 for רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a rabbinic-level impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garment ruling seems to show that absorbed Torah-level blood does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is דם תבוסה, which is only rabbinic, so it is a special leniency. Torah-level absorbed liquids still count.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה about absorbed liquid
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ quotes a משנה: absorbed liquid that cannot come out is טהור. That implies absorbed liquid that can come out is טמא, even before it comes out. This seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ challenged רבי יוחנן: 'Anything absorbed that cannot come out is טהור.' This implies that if it can come out, it is טמא, even though it has not come out yet!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ goes on the attack. He brings a משנה that seems to support his own view against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says outright that liquid which cannot come out is טהור. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ reads the flip side out of it: if the liquid can come out, it is טמא right now, even while it is still inside. That fits his view, and it seems to go against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Absorbed; soaked into something, like blood soaked into a garment
Able to come out (for example, by washing)
'But this implies…'; it introduces the flip-side reading of a text
Even though

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
phrases.notes: He is quoting a משנה from אהלות (3:2).

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַבָּלוּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לָצֵאת — טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: Anything absorbed that is unable to come out is pure.
This implies that if it is able to come out, it is impure,
even though it has not come out!
phrases.notes: This last line is רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's own point. The משנה itself does not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Earlier, רבי יוחנן challenged רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ and was answered. Now the roles flip, and רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view about absorbed liquid that has not come out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The flip side of the משנה says liquid that is able to come out is already טמא before it comes out. That goes against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב פפא: the two cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings in a new factor: whether the owner cares (הקפיד) about the absorbed liquid. If it cannot come out and he does not care, everyone says טהור. If it can come out and he does care, everyone says טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Whenever the liquid cannot come out and the owner does not care about it, everyone agrees it is טהור. When it can come out and he cares about it, everyone agrees it is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts to defend רבי יוחנן by listing the cases where the two sages do not argue at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא adds a second question: does the owner mind having this liquid in his garment? Once we know there is a case where everyone agrees it is טמא, the משנה's 'able to come out, so טמא' might be talking about that case. Then it is no proof against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He cared about it; the owner minds it and wants it out
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Anywhere that it is unable to come out,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִקְפִּיד עָלָיו — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל טָהוֹר;
phrases.english: and he did not care about it, everyone agrees it is pure;
phrases.notes: 'He' is the owner of the garment. The question is whether he minds having this liquid soaked in.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לָצֵאת וְהִקְפִּיד עָלָיו — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל טָמֵא.
phrases.english: if it is able to come out and he cared about it, everyone agrees it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לָצֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the challenge in step 15 by narrowing where רבי יוחנן and רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ actually disagree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): it adds the factor of whether the owner cares
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any absorbed liquid that is able to come out is טמא, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a case everyone agrees is טמא: when the owner cares. So the משנה need not go against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב פפא: the one case where they argue
steps.stepSummary: The real argument is only when the liquid can come out but the owner does not care. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says that since it can come out, it is טמא anyway. רבי יוחנן's reasoning begins, 'even though it can come out…', and continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue when it can come out and he does not care. One sage (רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ) holds: since it can come out, even though he does not care, it is טמא. The other sage (רבי יוחנן) holds: even though it can come out…
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now points to the single middle case where the two sages really disagree, and starts to give each one's reasoning. רבי יוחנן's reason is cut off here and finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, being able to come out is enough to make it טמא, and the owner's attitude does not matter. For רבי יוחנן, being able to come out is not enough on its own. The words 'even though it can come out' show that the owner not caring will be his reason for טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: When they argue; it points to the exact case of the disagreement
One sage holds… (literally 'the master holds')
Since; it gives the reason for a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of a sentence. רבי יוחנן's full reasoning, and his ruling of טהור, comes in the next section.

phrases.english: When they argue is where it is able to come out
and he did not care about it.
One sage holds: since it is able to come out,
phrases.notes: This first sage is רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ. He will say it is טמא.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הִקְפִּיד עָלָיו,
phrases.english: even though he did not care about it, it is impure.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּיָכוֹל לָצֵאת
phrases.english: And the other sage holds: even though it is able to come out…
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן. His sentence finishes in the next section.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי דְּיָכוֹל לָצֵאת וְלֹא הִקְפִּיד עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It finishes רב פפא's sorting of the cases by naming the one case where they actually argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the exact case of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sages argue about every case of liquid that is able to come out.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only when the liquid can come out and the owner does not care about it.
